title: Residue differential of a Betti-rank model
statement: Let \(W\) be a scheme, \(w\in W\), \(E\in D(\mathcal O_W)\), and fix derived localizations for all schemes and all localized open module sites [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-derived-category]. Assume all derived fibre cohomology spaces \(H^j(Li_w^*E)\) are finite dimensional over \(\kappa(w)\) [def-sc-derived-fiber-betti, def-weil-residue-field]. Let \(U\) be an affine open containing \(w\), and \(K\) a bounded cochain complex on the localized module site over \(U\). Assume \(E|_U\cong Q(K)\) and for every \(j\), \(K^j\cong\mathcal O_U^{\beta_j(E,w)}\). Let \(m\in\mathbf N\) and let \(e_1:\Gamma(U,K^1)\cong\Gamma(W,U)^m\) be any linear frame. Then for every \(t\in\Gamma(U,K^0)\) and \(i\in\operatorname{Fin}(m)\), the evaluation at \(w\) of the \(i\)-th coordinate of \(e_1(d_K^0(t))\) is zero. This is a residue calculation for a given model; it makes no assertion about a direct image, construction of a model, targets, negative Betti numbers or rank one in degree zero.

source.place: Tags 0BCD, minimal finite free residue model, and 0BF2, first source complex

proof.text: Transport K through the exact localized-site equivalence to modules on the scheme U. Because it is bounded and finite free it is K-flat. Termwise residue pullback therefore computes the derived fibre. The canonical factorization of the residue point through U and exact open restriction identify its cohomology, with its kappa(w)-linear scalar action, with derivedFiberCohomology W E j w. This is the stalk-free residue cohomology comparison applied to the given bounded free representative.

The given free term isomorphisms identify each term dimension in the residue complex with beta_j. Rank-nullity and the dimension formula for a quotient identify that dimension with the cohomology dimension plus the ranks of its two adjacent differentials. Both ranks must be zero. In particular the outgoing degree-zero differential is zero.

Tensor the section frame e1 with kappa(w). Its inverse tensors to an inverse, so it is a residue frame. Naturality of coordinate maps and residue extension identifies the coordinates of the residue differential on the residue of t with evaluation of the coordinates of d(t). The coefficient homomorphism is W.evaluation U w hwU. Since the differential is zero, every coordinate is zero, also when m=0.

theorem residueRankModel_differential_eval_eq_zero
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{v},
      HasDerivedCategory.{v + 1} (SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ (Y : Scheme.{v}) (U : Y.Opens), HasDerivedCategory.{v + 1}
      (SheafOfModules.{v} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (W : Scheme.{v}) (E : schemeDerivedCategory W) (w : W)
    (hfin : ∀ j : ℤ, Module.Finite (W.residueField w) (derivedFiberCohomology W E j w))
    (U : W.Opens) (hwU : w ∈ U) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{v} ((moduleRings W.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, j < a ∨ b < j → IsZero (K.X j))
    (hrank : ∀ j : ℤ, Nonempty (K.X j ≅ SheafOfModules.free
      (R := (moduleRings W.toRingedSpace).over U)
      (ULift.{v} (Fin (derivedFiberBetti W E j w)))))
    (he : Nonempty ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{v}
      (moduleRings W.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj K))
    (m : ℕ)
    (e1 : (K.X 1).val.obj (.op (Over.mk (𝟙 U))) ≃ₗ[Γ(W, U)] (Fin m → Γ(W, U)))
    (t : (K.X 0).val.obj (.op (Over.mk (𝟙 U)))) :
    ∀ i, W.evaluation U w hwU
      (e1 ((K.d 0 1).val.app (.op (Over.mk (𝟙 U))) t) i) = 0
